query: Prepare a one-page briefing for a meeting with Canva on 17 November 2026. Cover what changed in the last 30 days (news, launches, hires, deals), cite a source URL for every fact, and end with three open questions to ask.
briefing:
# Canva Briefing: Changes from 16 October to 15 November 2026

Prepared for the meeting on 17 November 2026. Items are limited to the window and include only facts with a source URL. Unverified items are flagged.

## Headline Change: Restructuring and Job Cuts

Canva announced its first-ever round of job cuts on 3 November 2026. CEO Melanie Perkins said 1,271 people, or 22% of staff, will lose their jobs, change roles or relocate [2]. Canva has not said how many will lose jobs [3]. Press coverage dates the announcement to 4 November [3][4]. Perkins said growth "has slowed for the first time in a decade" [4]. Canva cut its 2026 revenue growth forecast from 30% to 20% and earlier investors cut its valuation to about US$35 billion [4]. BBC reports a different figure, a drop from A$60bn to about A$49bn [5]. These valuation figures conflict across sources and should be confirmed before the meeting.

Changes:
- Product, Growth and Platform merge into one Product Org [2].
- Subspecialisation is reduced and layers are collapsed [2].
- Sydney becomes the primary home for more product teams. Hybrid staff are expected in the office 2 to 3 days a week from January [2][3].

Support for leavers: at least six months' salary regardless of location, removal of the one-year vesting cliff for recent joiners, twelve months of healthcare where provided, and a US$10,000 Canva Collective Fund grant (registration closes 14 December) [2][3]. Perkins said the company is "refounding" around small, empowered teams [2][6].

## News

- **3 Nov 2026:** Perkins's team update was published on the newsroom [2][1].
- **Mid-Oct to early Nov:** Canva's Ad Council and Common Sense Media partnerships, and the "What Will You Canva Today?" campaign, are listed in the newsroom index [1]. The campaign replaces the homepage question used for about 13 years and is Canva's first North American brand campaign [11].

## Product Launches

- **15 Oct 2026:** Digital literacy lessons for Canva Education, and the Mattel template collection [1].
- **21 Oct 2026:** Canva Research introduced [1].
- **22 Oct 2026:** Canva Craft, Canva's first image-generation model, was launched. Canva says it ranks as the world's second most advanced image-generation lab on DesignArena [1].
- **29 Oct 2026:** Canva Brush, a vision-language model for design, is powering supported edits for Pro subscribers. Canva says it is up to 69% faster and 46% lower cost per edit than its previous design agent. These figures are Canva's own claims [7][8]. Wider availability is "coming soon" [7].
- **3 Nov 2026:** Affinity for iPad launched in the App Store. Core tools are free for individuals. Canva AI Studio features require a Canva premium account [9]. The Affinity product page states that content is not used to train AI features [10].

## Hires and Departures

No executive appointments or departures were verified within the window. The only leadership-related item is the restructuring memo, which names no executives [2]. Dana Marineau, Canva's North American CMO, joined in April, which is outside the window [11].

## Deals, Partnerships and Investments

No new deals, acquisitions or funding rounds were verified within the window. The Klaviyo expanded integration (16 April 2026) and the Nitro bundle (May 2025) fall outside the window. A PayPal Payment Links deal with Canva was found, but its date could not be confirmed, so it is omitted.

## Open Questions for Canva

1. With the Product Org merged and layers reduced, who will own Brush, Craft and Affinity roadmaps, and when will Brush reach wider availability beyond Canva Pro?
2. The growth forecast was cut to 20% due to AI costs [4]. Brush reports 46% lower cost per edit [7]. How will these cost gains affect pricing and the Canva AI tiers?
3. Which partnerships and channel deals remain priorities after the restructuring, given that no new in-window deals have been announced?

### Sources

[1] Canva Newsroom: https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news
[2] An important update on our team (Canva Newsroom): https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/canva-team-update
[3] Canva CEO memo, Business Insider: https://www.businessinsider.com/canva-reorganization-layoffs-ceo-memo-2026-11
[4] Canva lays off over 1,200 people amid slowing growth, TechCrunch: https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/04/canva-lays-off-over-1200-people-amid-slowing-growth

30K views | Canva is laying off 1,271 employees. But its exit package is getting people talking. 👀

The company is restructuring 22% of its workforce after its revenue growth forecast dropped from 30% to 20%.

But here's what makes this different: departing employees will receive at least six months of salary, up to 12 months of health insurance, career coaching and one year of LinkedIn Premium.

They can even keep their company MacBooks. And employees looking to start their own businesses can apply for a $10,000 grant without giving Canva any equity.

Why go this far?

Because layoffs don't just affect the people leaving. They can also impact the morale and trust of employees who stay, along with the company's reputation.

Research cited in this discussion suggests that layoffs can damage a company's brand for weeks, while employees who perceive the process as fair tend to show greater commitment.

Canva is showing that how a company handles layoffs matters just as much as the decision itself.

Would you call this a better way to handle layoffs?
